categories.bengali_vocabulary: Bengali vocabulary — mon ambiguity, go particle, script false friends

categories.tamil_vocabulary: Tamil vocabulary — kaadhal, nee, vaan, malarndu

lines.gold_direct: O [girl], the moon is setting
lines.gold_natural: O girl, the moon is setting
lines.known_failure: model translates ni as 'no' or 'alas', or addresses the moon instead of listener
lines.notes: ni = female vocative particle; chann = moon; dhalna = to set/decline

lines.native: نی کرنے وے ہجر دی میں گل نہ
lines.roman: ni karne ve hijr di main gall nah
lines.gold_direct: O [girl], do not speak of separation, O [man]
lines.gold_natural: O girl, don't speak of parting
lines.known_failure: ni→'alas'/'no'; wrong actor (model says 'I shall not speak' instead of addressing listener); hijr→'distance'
lines.notes: ni = address to female listener; ve = address to male; gall nah = do not speak

lines.gold_direct: O [girl], I am turning back
lines.known_failure: ni→'no'/'alas'; valna→'wander'/'leave' instead of 'turn back'; 'ni main' read as 'no, I' creating wrong negation
lines.notes: valna specifically means to turn back/return; ni is vocative not negation

lines.native: نی میں جانا جوگیاں دے نال
lines.roman: ni main jaana jogiyan de naal
lines.gold_direct: O [girl], I want to go with the mystics
lines.gold_natural: O girl, I want to go with the mystics
lines.known_failure: hint causes ni to negate 'jaana' → 'I will NOT go' (opposite meaning); baseline→'alas, I will go'
lines.notes: REGRESSION CASE: Punjabi hint makes this worse by causing ni to negate the verb

lines.native: وے میں کیہ جاناں میں کون
lines.roman: ve main ki jaana main kaun
lines.gold_direct: O [man], what do I know of who I am
lines.gold_natural: O man, what do I know of who I am
lines.known_failure: ve→'alas'; 'ki jaana' read as 'how do I know' (acceptable variant) or 'I don't know'
lines.notes: ve = male vocative; ki jaana = what do I know (rhetorical)

lines.native: دل نوں کی سمجھاواں وے میں سجنا؟
lines.roman: dil nun ki samjhavan ve main sajna?
lines.gold_direct: How do I make the heart understand, O beloved?
lines.gold_natural: How do I make the heart understand, O beloved?
lines.known_failure: ve dropped or 'samjhana' mistranslated as 'console' or 'explain' instead of 'make understand'
lines.notes: samjhana has range: explain, make understand, convince; 'make understand' most literal

lines.gold_direct: O [girl], the moon has gone mad
lines.gold_natural: O girl, the moon has lost its mind
lines.known_failure: model addresses moon: 'O moon, you have gone mad'; or ni→'alas'; kamla→'crazy'(OK) or 'stupid'
lines.notes: ni is still addressing listener, not the moon; chann is subject not addressee

lines.gold_direct: O [girl], the moon has risen in the sky
lines.gold_natural: O girl, the moon has risen in the sky
lines.known_failure: model addresses moon or uses 'alas'
lines.notes: charha = has risen; asmane = in the sky

lines.gold_direct: My beloved comes, O [girl], my beloved comes
lines.gold_natural: My beloved comes, O girl, my beloved comes
lines.known_failure: model reads 'ni' as negation between repetitions → 'my beloved does not come'
lines.notes: HARD CASE: ni here is a discourse particle between repetitions (exclamatory), not negation; aave = comes (not 'does not come')

lines.native: سجنا وے، کیوں چھڈ گئے مینوں
lines.roman: sajna ve, kyon chhadd gaye mainu
lines.gold_direct: O beloved, why did you leave me
lines.gold_natural: O beloved, why did you leave me
lines.known_failure: usually correct — sajna is well-known; included as control
lines.notes: CONTROL: should pass easily. If model fails, it has regressed.

lines.gold_direct: a new respite
lines.known_failure: mohlat→'chance', 'opportunity', 'time', 'moment'; none of these capture the meaning of an extension/reprieve
lines.notes: mohlat = a granted extension of time, reprieve, respite — specifically implies time given by another

lines.native: اس پیار کو ہے صدیاں کافی نہیں
lines.roman: is pyaar ko hai sadiyan kaafi nahin
lines.gold_direct: centuries are not enough for this love
lines.gold_natural: centuries aren't enough for this love
lines.known_failure: sadiyan→'ages', 'eternity', 'eons', 'years' — all lose the precise plural-centuries meaning
lines.notes: sadiyan = plural of sadi (century); not a vague time word

lines.native: چل دیے تم کہاں نیر بھرنے کے یہاں
lines.roman: chal diye tum kahan neer bharne ke yahan
lines.gold_direct: where have you gone to fill water here
lines.gold_natural: where have you gone to fill water here
lines.known_failure: neer→'tears', 'river', 'stream'; correct is simply 'water'
lines.notes: neer is a poetic/Sanskrit-origin word for water (Urdu/Punjabi usage)

lines.gold_direct: why do marks remain
lines.known_failure: nishan→'scars' (too specific — implies physical wound), 'memories' (too abstract)
lines.notes: nishan = mark, trace, sign; in context of restless heart, likely emotional marks/traces

lines.gold_direct: the night of separation
lines.known_failure: hijr→'distance', 'longing', 'being far'; correct is 'separation' (classical Urdu term)
lines.notes: hijr is a classical Urdu/Persian term specifically for separation from beloved; not generic distance

lines.native: اکھیاں نے رواں، نی میں ولنا
lines.roman: akhiyan ne ravan, ni main valna
lines.gold_direct: the eyes are weeping, O [girl], I am turning back
lines.gold_natural: eyes weeping, O girl, I turn back
lines.known_failure: valna→'wander', 'leave', 'go'; correct is 'turn back' (implies reversal of direction)
lines.notes: valna = to turn back, to return; ravan = weeping/flowing (not the demon Ravan)

lines.gold_direct: yes, how naive I am
lines.known_failure: naadaan→'foolish', 'stupid', 'dumb'; correct is 'naive'/'innocent' (ignorant of worldly ways, not intellectually deficient)
lines.notes: naadaan = one who does not know; implies innocence/naivety not stupidity

lines.native: تو ویسے میرے دل میں سجا ہے
lines.roman: tu vaise mere dil mein saja hai
lines.gold_direct: you are adorned like that in my heart
lines.gold_natural: you are adorned in my heart like that
lines.known_failure: saja→'placed', 'sitting', 'residing'; correct is 'adorned'/'decorated' (aesthetic, not positional)
lines.notes: saja hai = is adorned/decorated; from sajana (to decorate, embellish)

lines.gold_direct: of this restless heart
lines.known_failure: dil-e-bechain→'heart of restlessness' (noun-of-noun) instead of 'restless heart' (adjective-noun)
lines.notes: izafat X-e-Y = Y modifies X; bechain = restless; dil = heart; so: restless heart

lines.gold_direct: heartache
lines.known_failure: 'pain of the heart' is acceptable; 'dard of dil' (untranslated) is a failure
lines.notes: dard = pain/ache; dil = heart; dard-e-dil = heartache (established compound)

lines.gold_direct: night of separation
lines.known_failure: shab→'darkness'/'evening' instead of 'night'; firaq (separation) confused with firaq (worry/concern)
lines.notes: shab = night; firaq = separation (cf. hijr — both mean separation but different registers)

lines.native: اس پیار کو ہے صدیاں کافی نہیں
lines.roman: is pyaar ko hai sadiyan kaafi nahin
lines.gold_direct: centuries are not enough for this love
lines.gold_natural: centuries aren't enough for this love
lines.known_failure: model adds 'our love', 'my love', 'your love'; original specifies only 'this love'
lines.notes: pyaar ko = for this love; no possessive specified; must not introduce one

lines.gold_direct: the heart cannot join again
lines.gold_natural: the heart can't come back together
lines.known_failure: model adds 'our hearts', 'my heart', 'your heart'; original says 'the heart' (abstract)
lines.notes: dil = the heart (not my/your/our); ambiguity is poetic — must be preserved

lines.native: یہ پلکوں میں کچھ باتیں ہیں
lines.roman: ye palkon mein kuch baatein hain
lines.gold_direct: there are some words in these eyelids
lines.gold_natural: there are words in these eyelids
lines.known_failure: model adds 'hidden' (inference), 'my eyelids', 'your eyelids', or converts to 'unspoken words'
lines.notes: palkon = eyelids/lashes (not eyes); baatein = words/things; no possessive; no hidden/unspoken

lines.gold_direct: you, in that case, just ask
lines.known_failure: model adds 'me', 'from me', 'for it'; original leaves object unspecified
lines.notes: maang le = ask/request/take; no object specified; do not introduce one

lines.gold_direct: of this restless heart
lines.known_failure: model forces complete sentence: 'this restless heart longs for you'; correct is fragment ending with 'of'
lines.notes: ke = of/belonging to; this is a genitive fragment that continues into next line (aansu mere nain ke)

lines.gold_direct: the tears of my eyes
lines.known_failure: model adds verb: 'my eyes shed tears', 'tears fall from my eyes'; correct is noun phrase only
lines.notes: aansu = tears; nain ke = of the eyes; this is the second half of a compound fragment

lines.native: اور آسماں میں جو تارے ہیں
lines.roman: aur aasmaan mein jo taare hain
lines.gold_direct: and the stars in the sky
lines.gold_natural: and the stars in the sky
lines.known_failure: model adds predicate: 'and the stars in the sky shine', 'watch over us'; correct ends at 'sky' — relative clause with no conclusion
lines.notes: jo taare hain = the stars that are; sentence continues into next line (tu vaise mere dil mein saja hai)

lines.gold_direct: so ask like this
lines.known_failure: model adds object 'ask for it/me/that'; or adds softener 'won't you ask' (converts statement to question)
lines.notes: 'na' here is a softening particle (like 'please/won't you') not negation

lines.gold_direct: the eyes are weeping
lines.known_failure: ravan confused with 'Ravan' (the demon king from Ramayana) or 'ravan' misread as 'gone'
lines.notes: ravan in Punjabi = weeping, flowing (of tears); completely unrelated to Sanskrit Ravana

lines.gold_direct: in a moment I would melt
lines.gold_natural: in just a moment I'd melt
lines.known_failure: pighal→'disappear', 'dissolve', 'fade', 'crumble'; correct is 'melt' (literal heat/emotion sense)
lines.notes: pighal = to melt (wax, ice, or used metaphorically for emotional yielding)

lines.gold_direct: listen to my words
lines.known_failure: gal→'cheek' (Hindi/Urdu gal = cheek) but in Punjabi gal/gall = words, talk, matter
lines.notes: gal/gall in Punjabi = words, talk, speech (completely different from Urdu/Hindi gal = cheek)

lines.gold_direct: O [girl], the moon is setting
lines.gold_natural: O girl, the moon is setting
lines.known_failure: chann confused with 'chain' (peace/restfulness in Urdu) instead of moon (Punjabi chann = moon)
lines.notes: chann in Punjabi = moon; chain in Urdu = peace; different words, different languages

lines.gold_direct: the tears of my eyes
lines.known_failure: nain→'nine' (English false friend) or 'nain' left untranslated; correct is 'eyes'
lines.notes: nain/naina = eyes (poetic Urdu/Punjabi); aansu = tears

lines.native: سجنا وے، کیوں چھڈ گئے مینوں
lines.roman: sajna ve, kyon chhadd gaye mainu
lines.gold_direct: O beloved, why did you leave me
lines.gold_natural: O beloved, why did you leave me
lines.known_failure: none expected — control line
lines.notes: sajna is well-known; this should pass without any hint or glossary

lines.native: یہ ادھوری سی ساری راتیں ہیں
lines.roman: ye adhoori si saari raatein hain
lines.gold_direct: all the nights are somewhat incomplete
lines.gold_natural: every night feels a little incomplete
lines.known_failure: none expected — control line
lines.notes: adhoori = incomplete; si = somewhat/a little; raatein = nights

lines.gold_direct: I will ask from God
lines.known_failure: none expected — control line
lines.notes: khuda = God; maang loon = I will ask/request

lines.gold_direct: yes, how naive I am
lines.known_failure: naadaan→'foolish' is the only common failure; otherwise control
lines.notes: naadaan = naive/innocent; haan = yes

lines.gold_direct: my heart, O [girl], does not agree
lines.gold_natural: O girl, my heart won't agree
lines.known_failure: ni mid-sentence treated as negation: 'my heart doesn't agree at all'; correct is ni = vocative inserted mid-statement
lines.notes: ni appears mid-sentence as a discourse particle to the listener

lines.gold_direct: O [girl], I am crazy
lines.known_failure: ni→'alas'/'no'; 'kamli' could be translated as 'stupid' (wrong register) — should be 'crazy'/'mad'/'lovestruck'
lines.notes: kamli = crazy/lovestruck (feminine form of kamla); a Sufi term for divine madness

lines.gold_direct: O [man], I have reconciled with my beloved
lines.gold_natural: O man, I've made peace with my beloved
lines.known_failure: ve dropped; yaar→'friend' (correct in colloquial but 'beloved' is better in song context); mana liya→'pleased' or 'convinced'
lines.notes: mana liya = reconciled/appeased/won over; yaar = beloved/friend

lines.gold_direct: listen, O beloved, to my words
lines.gold_natural: listen, O beloved, to my words
lines.known_failure: gal→'cheek' (wrong language); ve dropped; correct: gal = words in Punjabi
lines.notes: sun = listen; ve = male vocative; sajna = beloved; gal = words/talk (Punjabi)

lines.native: جا وے جا، نہ ستا مینوں
lines.roman: ja ve ja, nah sata mainu
lines.gold_direct: go, O [man], go, do not trouble me
lines.gold_natural: go, just go, don't trouble me
lines.known_failure: ve dropped; 'sata' mistranslated as 'disturb'/'bother' (acceptable variants exist)
lines.notes: ja = go; ve = male vocative; sata = trouble/torment; mainu = me

lines.gold_direct: where is there peace for me
lines.known_failure: chain→ English 'chain' (metal links); correct is 'peace/rest' (Urdu/Hindi چین)
lines.notes: chain (चैन) = peace, rest, tranquility — false cognate with English 'chain'

lines.song: Jab Tak Hai Jaan (A.R. Rahman / Gulzar)
lines.gold_direct: as long as there is life
lines.known_failure: jaan→'John' (name), or left as 'jaan'; correct is 'life' or 'soul'
lines.notes: jaan = life, soul — highly polysemous; in this title means 'as long as life remains'

lines.gold_direct: just one moment
lines.known_failure: lamha→'lamba' (long/tall) which is wrong; lamha = moment (Arabic lahn origin)
lines.notes: lamha (لمحہ) = moment; not to be confused with lamba (लम्बा) = long/tall

lines.gold_direct: you and I in passionate love
lines.known_failure: ishq translated as 'love' without distinction from pyaar; ishq implies passionate/consuming love (Arabic origin, stronger register)
lines.notes: ishq (عشق) = passionate consuming love; pyaar = affectionate love; mohabbat = devotional love — all translated 'love' but distinct

lines.gold_direct: if only they were here
lines.known_failure: 'hote' read as simple past 'they were' instead of counterfactual 'if only they were'
lines.notes: kaash + subjunctive = counterfactual wish; 'hote' here is subjunctive not past indicative

lines.gold_direct: whether or not there is a tomorrow
lines.known_failure: kal→'yesterday' (kal means both yesterday and tomorrow); in context clearly 'tomorrow'; 'ho na ho' = may or may not be
lines.notes: kal (कल) = yesterday AND tomorrow (determined by context); 'ho na ho' is subjunctive negation — 'may be or may not be'

lines.native: हर तरफ तू ही तू है
lines.roman: har taraf tu hi tu hai
lines.gold_direct: in every direction, only you exist
lines.known_failure: taraf→'traffic' or left untranslated; taraf = direction, side; 'tu hi tu' = only you
lines.notes: taraf (طرف) = direction, side, towards; har taraf = everywhere/in every direction

lines.song: Ae Dil Hai Mushkil (Arijit Singh / Pritam)
lines.gold_direct: O heart, it is difficult
lines.gold_natural: O heart, how hard this is
lines.known_failure: ae→'hey' (too casual) or dropped; mushkil→'muscle-y'/'hard' without the Urdu connotation of emotional difficulty
lines.notes: ae (اے) = O (vocative, like 'ae dil' = O heart); mushkil = difficult/hard (Arabic root)

lines.song: Phir Le Aya Dil (Arijit Singh / Barfi)
lines.gold_direct: the heart brought me back again
lines.gold_natural: the heart brought me back again
lines.known_failure: phir→'fear' (English false friend); or model adds reason not in this line
lines.notes: phir = again, once more; 'dil le aaya' = heart brought (dil is subject, mujhe = me is object)

lines.gold_direct: let the heart beat
lines.known_failure: model adds 'my heart', 'your heart'; original leaves possessive unspecified
lines.notes: 'dil' here is unspecified — not my/your/our; dhadakne do = let it beat (infinitive + do = causative-let)

lines.gold_direct: intoxicated wandering mystic
lines.known_failure: mast→English 'mast' (a pole/satisfied); qalandar→'calendar'; correct: mast = spiritually intoxicated/ecstatic; qalandar = wandering Sufi mystic
lines.notes: mast (مست) = intoxicated, ecstatic (used of Sufi spiritual states); qalandar = a specific type of itinerant Sufi dervish

lines.native: जो बीत गई सो बात गई
lines.roman: jo beet gayi so baat gayi
lines.song: Harivansh Rai Bachchan / common Hindi verse
lines.gold_direct: what has passed, that matter has passed
lines.known_failure: model adds 'my past' or 'our story'; original is impersonal — no subject specified
lines.notes: jo/so = what/that (correlative pair); no subject or possessive — deliberately universal/impersonal

lines.gold_direct: the string of the eyes
lines.known_failure: dor→'door' (English false friend); dor = string, thread, cord — 'aankhon ki dor' = the gaze-string connecting two people
lines.notes: dor (डोर/ڈور) = string, thread, kite-string; 'aankhon ki dor' is a poetic image: the invisible string of a gaze

lines.native: प्राण जाएँ पर वचन न जाएँ
lines.roman: pran jaaye par vachan na jaaye
lines.gold_direct: let life go but a promise must not go
lines.gold_natural: life may be lost but never a vow
lines.known_failure: pran→'pray' or 'prayer'; pran = life, vital breath, soul
lines.notes: pran (प्राण) = life, vital force, breath of life (Sanskrit origin); vachan = word, vow, promise

lines.gold_direct: when you are found / if you are met
lines.known_failure: 'mile' read as English 'mile' (distance unit); correct: 'mile' is subjunctive of 'milna' (to meet/be found)
lines.notes: 'tu jo mile' = you, when found/met (subjunctive jo-clause); 'milna' = to meet, encounter, receive

lines.native: رنجش ہی سہی، دل ہی دکھانے کے لیے آ
lines.roman: ranjish hi sahi, dil hi dukhaane ke liye aa
lines.song: Ranjish Hi Sahi (Mehdi Hassan / Faiz Ahmed Faiz)
lines.gold_direct: even if it is bitterness, come to break the heart
lines.gold_natural: even bitterness — come, if only to hurt
lines.known_failure: ranjish→'illness', 'anger', 'jealousy'; correct is 'bitterness/grudge' — a specific emotional residue after conflict
lines.notes: ranjish (رنجش) = bitterness, a residual grievance; not anger (gussa) or jealousy (hasad)

lines.native: مجھ سے پہلی سی محبت میری محبوب نہ مانگ
lines.roman: mujh se pehli si mohabbat meri mahboob na maang
lines.song: Mujh Se Pehli Si (Faiz Ahmed Faiz / Iqbal Bano)
lines.gold_direct: do not ask of me that first love, my beloved
lines.gold_natural: don't ask me for that first love, my beloved
lines.known_failure: mahboob treated as a male name (Mahmood/Mahboob); it is a direct address: 'O beloved'
lines.notes: mahboob (محبوب) = beloved (can be m/f); used here as vocative address — 'O my beloved'

lines.native: اور بھی دکھ ہیں زمانے میں محبت کے سوا
lines.roman: aur bhi dukh hain zamane mein mohabbat ke siwa
lines.song: Mujh Se Pehli Si (Faiz Ahmed Faiz)
lines.gold_direct: there are other sorrows in the world besides love
lines.gold_natural: the world holds sorrows beyond love
lines.known_failure: siwa→'Shiva' (Hindu deity); siwa = besides/apart from/except
lines.notes: siwa (سوا) = besides, apart from, other than; zamane = of the age/world/era

lines.native: ہزاروں خواہشیں ایسی کہ ہر خواہش پہ دم نکلے
lines.roman: hazaron khwaishein aisi ke har khwaish pe dam nikle
lines.gold_direct: thousands of such desires that on each desire, a breath escapes
lines.gold_natural: a thousand such desires — each one takes my breath
lines.known_failure: khwaish→'wish' (undersells it); dam nikle→'I die' (too strong); khwaish = yearning/desire with intensity; dam nikle = breath escapes (sighing/dying for each)
lines.notes: khwaish (خواہش) = desire, yearning (stronger/more literary than 'wish'); dam = breath/life; dam nikalna = for breath to escape (sigh, die a little)

lines.native: حسنِ یار پہ کیا جان نثار نہ کریں
lines.roman: husn-e-yaar pe kya jaan nisar na karein
lines.gold_direct: why should we not sacrifice our life for the beauty of the beloved
lines.gold_natural: how can we not give our life for the beloved's beauty
lines.known_failure: husn-e-yaar→'husn of yaar' (untranslated); or 'the goodness of the friend' (husn also = goodness, but here clearly beauty); yaar = beloved/friend
lines.notes: husn-e-yaar = beauty of the beloved (izafat: husn + e + yaar); jaan nisar = life-sacrifice

lines.gold_direct: night of sorrow
lines.known_failure: shab→'shadow', 'Shab' (name); shab = night (Persian); gham = sorrow/grief; together = night of grief
lines.notes: shab (شب) = night (Persian); gham (غم) = sorrow, grief; shab-e-gham = a night spent in sorrow — classical ghazal image

lines.gold_direct: soul of my soul
lines.known_failure: jaan-e-jaan→'the life/soul's life' (awkward literal); or left as 'jaan-e-jaan'; correct: fixed phrase meaning 'soul of my soul' — highest term of endearment
lines.notes: jaan-e-jaan = soul of my soul; a superlative term of address for the beloved

lines.gold_direct: heartache
lines.known_failure: 'pain of the heart' is acceptable; 'dard of dil' (untranslated) is failure; 'heart's pain' also acceptable
lines.notes: dard (درد) = pain/ache; dil = heart; dard-e-dil = heartache — established compound with one-word English equivalent

lines.gold_direct: the heart/mind is not well
lines.gold_natural: the heart is not at ease
lines.known_failure: mon→'mind' only (loses heart connotation); mon→'man' (gender error); mon in Bengali = mind AND heart simultaneously — English must choose
lines.notes: mon (মন) covers what English splits into 'heart' (emotional seat) and 'mind' (mental state); both are valid depending on context; translator must choose and note the ambiguity

lines.gold_direct: where is your heart/mind
lines.known_failure: tomar→'tomato' (absurd but GPT-4o has done this); mon→'mind' only; correct: tomar = your; mon = heart/mind (both)
lines.notes: tomar (তোমার) = your (intimate/poetic second person); mon = heart/mind; 'where is your mind/heart' — context of a wandering beloved

lines.gold_direct: I know you, I know you
lines.gold_natural: I know you, I do know you
lines.known_failure: 'go' translated as 'go' (motion verb) or 'so'; 'go' here is a Bengali emphasis particle (like 'I do know'), not movement
lines.notes: 'go' (গো) in Bengali = an emphatic/expressive particle, not the verb 'to go'; chini = I know; tomare = you (accusative)

lines.gold_direct: the soul/life wants, the eyes do not want
lines.gold_natural: the soul longs but the eyes refuse
lines.known_failure: pran→'pray'/'prayer'; chokkhu→'chalk'/'choke'; pran = life/soul/vitality (Sanskrit); chokkhu = eyes
lines.notes: pran (প্রাণ) = life, soul, vital force (same root as Hindi pran); chokkhu (চোখ/চক্ষু) = eyes

lines.gold_direct: what does love mean

lines.notes: bhalobasha (ভালোবাসা) = love (noun); bhaloba+sha from 'bhalo' (good) + 'basha' (feeling/liking); mane (মানে) = meaning, means

lines.native: যদি তোর ডাক শুনে কেউ না আসে
lines.roman: jodi tor dak shune keu na aase
lines.gold_direct: if no one comes hearing your call
lines.gold_natural: if no one answers your call
lines.known_failure: model forces completion: 'if no one comes to hear your call, don't despair'; this is the conditional clause — its conclusion is the next line
lines.notes: jodi = if (conditional); tor = your (informal); dak = call/summons; shune = hearing; keu na aase = if no one comes; the apodosis (then...) is the next line 'ekla cholo re'

lines.gold_direct: then walk alone
lines.known_failure: 're' at end treated as negation or question marker; re here is an emphatic/vocative particle (like 'hey'); also 'ekla'→'ankle'
lines.notes: tobe = then; ekla = alone; cholo = walk/go (imperative); re (রে) = emphatic/expressive particle at end of Bengali exclamations/calls

lines.gold_direct: the sky full of sun and stars
lines.gold_natural: a sky full of sun and stars
lines.known_failure: akash→'a-cash'/'Akash' (name only); surya→'Surya' (name/deity only); akash = sky; surya = sun; tara = stars
lines.notes: akash (আকাশ) = sky; surya (সূর্য) = sun (Sanskrit origin); tara (তারা) = stars; these are common words that models sometimes leave untranslated or treat as proper nouns

lines.gold_direct: who are you to me
lines.known_failure: tumi → 'you' (OK) but model adds context: 'who are you to me, my love'; original is an open question
lines.notes: tumi = you (intimate second person, between aapni=formal and tui=very informal); amar ke = who to me — deliberately ambiguous question

lines.gold_direct: on the other side of the river
lines.known_failure: nodi→'no-dee' (gibberish) or untranslated; opare→'opera'; nodi = river; opare = on the other side/bank
lines.notes: nodi (নদী) = river; opare (ওপারে) = on the other side/bank/shore; a common Bengali lyric image of longing across a river

lines.gold_direct: there is a pleasure in losing one's way
lines.gold_natural: there is a sweetness in losing the way
lines.known_failure: shwad→'swad'/'sweat'; path→'path' (fine); harabar→'horrible'; shwad (স্বাদ) = taste, flavor, pleasure
lines.notes: path (পথ) = road/way; harabar (হারাবার) = of losing; shwad (স্বাদ) = taste, pleasure, relish — 'the pleasurable taste of getting lost'

lines.native: কে যাস রে ভাটি গাঙ বাইয়া
lines.roman: ke jas re bhati gang baiya
lines.gold_direct: who goes there, rowing downstream
lines.gold_natural: who goes there rowing down the river
lines.known_failure: 'bhati' → 'Bhati' (name/place) instead of 'downstream'; 'gang' → 'gang' (criminal group) instead of 'river'; re = emphatic particle (not negation)
lines.notes: bhati (ভাটি) = downstream/ebb; gang (গাং) = river (dialectal/folk Bengali); baiya = rowing; re = emphatic particle

lines.gold_direct: O heart
lines.known_failure: left untranslated as 'Nenjame'; neñjam = heart; -e suffix = Tamil vocative marker
lines.notes: neñjam (நெஞ்சம்) = heart; -e (ஏ) = vocative suffix in Tamil; Nenjame = O heart (direct address)

lines.gold_direct: O my life / O my soul
lines.known_failure: uyire→'hire' or untranslated; uyir = life/soul; -e = vocative suffix
lines.notes: uyir (உயிர்) = life, soul, vital breath; -e vocative = O; Uyire = O my life/soul — intimate term of address

lines.gold_direct: O wind, come
lines.known_failure: kaattre→'cattle' or untranslated; -e suffix missed; kaatru = wind; kaattre = O wind (vocative)
lines.notes: kaatru (காற்று) = wind/breeze; kaattre = O wind (vocative -e); vaa = come (imperative)

lines.gold_direct: what is love
lines.known_failure: kaadhal→'catholic' or left untranslated; endral = if/when said; enna = what; kaadhal = romantic love specifically
lines.notes: kaadhal (காதல்) = romantic/passionate love (more specific than English 'love'); anbu = love in broader sense; endral enna = literally 'if one says [it], what [does it mean]'

lines.gold_direct: the time when you are not there
lines.known_failure: 'nee' read as negation ('no' or 'not'); nee = you (informal); illatha = without/not having; neram = time
lines.notes: nee (நீ) = you (informal second person in Tamil); NOT a negation; 'illatha' (இல்லாத) = without/not-having; neram = time/moment

lines.gold_direct: sky rain / rain from the sky
lines.known_failure: vaan→'van' (vehicle); mazhai→'massage'/'mazai'; vaan = sky; mazhai = rain
lines.notes: vaan (வான்) = sky, heavens; mazhai (மழை) = rain; vaan mazhai = rain from the sky (poetic image)

lines.gold_direct: blooming and blooming
lines.known_failure: repetition read as copy error — model collapses to 'blooming'; or 'malar'→'malar' (name only); malarndu = having bloomed (gerund); repetition is intentional emphasis
lines.notes: malar (மலர்) = flower; malarndu = having bloomed (past participle/gerund); repetition (malarndu malarndu) = emphatic continuing action — NOT a typo

lines.gold_direct: O dear one, O graceful one
lines.known_failure: kanne→'cane' or 'cannon'; kalaimane→ untranslated; kann = eye (figurative term of endearment); -e = vocative; kalai = art; mane = one who embodies
lines.notes: kann (கண்) = eye; kanne (கண்ணே) = O eyes (vocative, term of endearment like 'O dear one'); kalaimane = one who embodies art/grace (compound vocative)

lines.song: Pasoori (Ali Sethi & Shae Gill / Coke Studio S14)
lines.gold_direct: my difficulty, O girl, my difficulty
lines.gold_natural: my plight, O girl, my plight
lines.known_failure: pasoori left untranslated; pasoori = difficulty, predicament, plight (Punjabi — specifically the tangle of coming and going)
lines.notes: pasoori (پسوری) = difficulty/plight/predicament — the specific anguish of an unresolved situation; ni = female vocative (O girl)

lines.gold_direct: I will set this helplessness on fire
lines.gold_natural: I'll set my helplessness on fire
lines.known_failure: majboori→'majority'; agg→'egg'/'ago'; majboori = helplessness, compulsion; agg = fire; lavan = set/apply
lines.notes: agg (اگ) = fire; lavan (لواں) = I set/apply; nu = to/onto; majboori (مجبوری) = helplessness, being forced/compelled — the state of having no choice

lines.gold_direct: O my beloved, of separations
lines.known_failure: dhol→'drum' (wrong — here dhol = term of endearment for beloved); judaiyaan→ untranslated; di = of
lines.notes: dhol (ڈھول) = drum (literal), but also used as a term of endearment in Punjabi folk (like 'my love/beloved'); judaiyaan (جدائیاں) = separations (plural of judai = separation)

lines.gold_direct: Bulha, what do I know of who I am
lines.gold_natural: Bulha, what do I know of who I am
lines.known_failure: 'ki jaana' read as 'why go' or 'what going'; Bulha = the poet addressing himself; ki jaana main kaun = what do I know of who I am (existential questioning)
lines.notes: Bulha (بُلھا) = nickname for Bulleh Shah (self-address); ki jaana (کی جاناں) = what do I know; main kaun = who am I; classic Sufi existential line

lines.native: کِنّا سوہنا تینوں ربّ نے بنایا

lines.gold_direct: how beautiful God has made you
lines.gold_natural: how beautifully God has made you

lines.notes: kinna (کِنّا) = how much/how; sohna (سوہنا) = beautiful (m.), sohni (f.); tainu = you (Punjabi accusative); rabb (ربّ) = God/Lord; banaya = made

lines.song: Punjabi folk / Shafqat Amanat Ali tradition
lines.gold_direct: the tears of the eyes do not stop

lines.notes: akhiyan (اکھیاں) = eyes (Punjabi); neer (نیر) = water/tears (poetic Punjabi/Sanskrit origin); thamde = that stop/are stilled; 'akhiyan de neer' = the water of the eyes = tears

lines.song: Afreen Afreen (Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan / Muzaffar Warsi)
lines.gold_direct: moon-browed / one whose forehead is like the moon

lines.notes: mah (ماہ) = moon (Persian); jabeen (جبیں) = forehead; mah-jabeen = moon-browed (poetic compound describing radiant beauty)

lines.native: حسنِ جاناں کی تعریف ممکن نہیں
lines.gold_direct: the beauty of the beloved cannot be praised/described
lines.gold_natural: the beloved's beauty is beyond description
lines.known_failure: husn-e-jaanaan→'husn of jaan' (close but jaanaan = beloved, not jaan = life/soul); ta'reef→'traffic'/'trade'; mumkin = possible
lines.notes: husn (حسن) = beauty; jaanaan (جاناں) = beloved (not jaan = life); ta'reef (تعریف) = praise, description; mumkin nahin = not possible

lines.native: چہرہ جیسے غزل، چہرہ جانِ غزل
lines.gold_direct: a face like a ghazal, a face that is the soul of the ghazal
lines.gold_natural: a face like a ghazal, the soul of the ghazal
lines.known_failure: jaan-e-ghazal→'the life of ghazal' (acceptable) or 'jaan of ghazal' (untranslated izafat); chehra = face; jaan = soul/life here means the essence
lines.notes: jaan-e-ghazal = soul/essence of the ghazal (izafat); the face is not just like a ghazal but is the very essence of one

lines.gold_direct: sigh of the helpless
lines.known_failure: bekas→'because' or 'be-cause'; aah = sigh; bekas = helpless/friendless (be = without + kas = someone); izafat connects them
lines.notes: aah (آہ) = sigh; bekas (بے کس) = without support, helpless, friendless (be = without, kas = anyone); aah-e-bekas = the sigh that comes from total helplessness

lines.gold_direct: that which cannot be said
lines.known_failure: model adds 'by me' or 'by you'; original is impersonal passive — speaker unspecified
lines.notes: passive construction in Hindi: 'bolajaata' = can be said (potential passive); 'jo bola nahin jaata' = that which cannot be spoken — no subject

lines.gold_direct: the heart breaks
lines.known_failure: model adds possessive: 'my heart breaks'; original is universal/impersonal — dil = the heart (unspecified)
lines.notes: dil here is used universally/impersonally (like 'the heart breaks' in English proverb); toota = broke/breaks; no possessive in original

lines.gold_direct: evening comes / evening falls
lines.known_failure: model adds time specification ('every evening', 'when evening comes') — original is a simple habitual/eternal present
lines.notes: hoti hai = habitual present (it happens, it is); shaam = evening; deliberately simple — do not add specificity

lines.gold_direct: when you will have gone away
lines.known_failure: model adds consequence not in this line: 'when you leave, I will be alone'; this is the temporal clause only
lines.notes: jab = when (temporal clause marker); jaaoge = will go (future); conclusion is in the next line — must not be added here

lines.gold_direct: those people who say

lines.notes: jo...hain = relative clause; log = people; kehte = who say; sentence continues into next line — fragment

lines.native: دل ہی تو ہے نہ سنگ و خشت

lines.notes: sang (سنگ) = stone (Persian; cf. 'sangstone'); khisht (خشت) = brick (Persian); 'sang o khisht' = stone and brick = cold unfeeling material

lines.gold_direct: the strings of the eyes / the gaze-strings
lines.known_failure: dor→'door' (English false cognate); dor = string, thread — here the invisible thread of a gaze
lines.notes: dor (ڈور) = string, thread, cord (of a kite, etc.); 'aankhon ke dor' = the gaze as a binding string — poetic image; NOT 'door'

lines.gold_direct: come if you have leisure / come if you are free
lines.known_failure: fursat→'first' or untranslated; fursat = leisure, free time, a moment of ease
lines.notes: fursat (فرصت) = leisure, free time, a spare moment — implies the beloved is always too busy; 'fursat ho' = if there is leisure/time

lines.gold_direct: heart met heart
lines.known_failure: mila→'mile' (English distance unit) or 'miller'; mila = met/found (past tense of milna); 'dil se dil mila' = hearts found each other
lines.notes: mila (मिला) = met, found, received (past tense of milna = to meet/find); NOT 'mile' the distance unit

lines.gold_direct: you are mine
lines.known_failure: none expected — simple possessive
lines.notes: tum = you (informal); mere = my/mine; ho = are (second person present); should pass without difficulty

lines.gold_direct: goodbye / may God protect you
lines.known_failure: none expected — well-known phrase
lines.notes: khuda = God; haafiz = protector/guardian; 'may God protect you' = goodbye

lines.gold_direct: I love you
lines.known_failure: none expected — simple and well-known
lines.notes: ami = I; tomai = you (accusative); bhalobasi = love (present tense verb); should pass everywhere
